answer: A stake-bonded reputation works like a pearl forming layer by layer: an agent must lock collateral and build a verifiable work history before it can trade, so creating a fake identity costs real money and time. Reputation peaks at its zenith only after sustained honest service, and a single proven fraud burns the bond instantly, like a comet that flares once and vanishes. An attacker needing thousands of aged, bonded identities faces a cost that grows faster than any reward from gaming the market.
